35.16818,-81.45042: Patrick Ferguson. Tory force led by Col. Ferguson camped nearby Oct. 4-5, 1780. Two days later Ferguson died in major British defeat at Kings Mountain, 5 mi. SE.
35.16829,-81.45029: Cornwallis. Entered North Carolina near here, January, 1781, on his second invasion of the state, pursuing Morgan and Greene.
35.1684,-81.45016: North Carolina South Carolina. NORTH CAROLINA / Colonized, 1585-87, by first English settlers in America; permanently settled c. 1650; first to vote readiness for independence, Apr. 12, 1776 b/w SOUTH CAROLINA / Formed in 1712 from part of Carolina, which was chartered in 1663, it was first settled by the English in 1670. One of the 13 original states.
35.18303,-81.41687: Kings Mountain Battleground. Site of decisive British defeat on Oct. 7, 1780. National Military Park located 5 mi. southeast in South Carolina.
35.25224,-81.03252: Goshen Presbyterian Church. Established in 1764. Rev. Humphrey Hunter, the first minister, arrived in 1796. Moved to present site, 2 mi. NW, in 1956.
35.2617,-81.19992: Loray Strike. A strike in 1929 at the Loray Mill, 200 yards S., left two dead and spurred opposition to labor unions statewide.
35.26226,-81.18398: R. Gregg Cherry. Governor of North Carolina, 1945-1949. State legislator. Promoted good roads and rural electrification. Grave is 3 miles S.E.
35.44276,-81.15548: Iron Works. Many iron mines and forges were operated within a radius of ten miles of this point between 1790 and 1880.
35.46186,-81.25382: Confederate Laboratory. Under Dr. A.S. Piggott, manufactured medicine for Confederacy, 1863-65. Remains are 2 mi. S.
35.46574,-81.26866: Connie M. Guion 1882 1971. Pioneer female physician. Gained national reputation from work at Cornell medical clinic, 1922-1970. Born 2/10 mile N.
35.46598,-81.08821: Machpelah Cemetery. Presbyterian, 1801. Graves include those of Alexander Brevard, Joseph & James Graham, and Robert Hall & Joseph Graham Morrison.
35.4667,-81.08578: Catawba Springs. Fashionable "watering place," a recreational and social center prior to 1861. The hotel stood five miles northeast.
35.46956,-81.2561: J. G. Arends. Native German, pioneer teacher and minister, ordained 1775, first president of the N.C. Lutheran Synod, 1803. Grave a few yds. east.
35.47115,-81.25767: Andre Michaux. French botanist, pioneer in studying flora of western North Carolina, passed through Lincolnton, July 24, Sept. 11, 1794, and April 29, 1795.
35.47265,-81.25785: U. D. C. Memorial Hall. Building housed first the Pleasant Retreat Academy, chartered 1813. Later public library, museum. 1 block east.
35.47291,-81.25227: William A. Hoke 1851 1925. Chief justice 1 year & assoc. justice 20 yrs., N.C. Supreme Court. Superior court judge 13 yrs. Birthplace stood here.
Stephen D. Ramseur. West Point graduate. A Confederate major general at 27; mortally wounded, Cedar Creek, Va. Grave 2 blocks N.
35.47415,-81.2582: Robert F. Hoke 1837 1912. Major general, C.S.A. Promoted after victory at Battle of Plymouth. Led troops in Va. & N.C. Home stands 50 yards E.
35.47455,-81.25847: Michael Hoke 1874 1944. Pioneer orthopedic surgeon; founded hospitals for crippled children; chief surgeon of Warm Springs (Ga.) Foundation. Birthplace 80 yds. east.
